decisions.reason: As a close extension of the established hardware range in a growing market, there is no clear sign it falls below aspiration levels, and a large firm with slack would usually give such a recent launch more time.

This door lever handle family fits the firm's broad system offering and budget-tier logic, so without evidence of underperformance management would retain it while learning from the first market period.
Because the product is near the firm's core design-led competence and no negative market signal is reported, the behavioral response is to continue rather than reallocate resources prematurely.
A newly launched handle design close to existing capabilities would normally be kept while management compares its results with internal aspirations and peer offerings over a longer horizon.
This handle family supports the firm's strategy of breadth across building complexity and price points, and absent evidence of a shortfall there is little reason to drop it after only one year.

The electronic access system is strongly aligned with the firm's move toward integrated digital building solutions and was launched with a differentiated feature, so management would be especially inclined to continue supporting it.
